question: Should OpenClaw support configurable ASR for native voice input as a core/native provider seam, and should the first milestone be macOS Push-to-Talk only or a broader custom-HTTP/cross-platform surface?
rationale: The implementation would add provider selection, credentials, microphone-audio network egress, private/local endpoint policy, and fallback semantics; those are maintainer product and security choices rather than a safe cleanup fix.

options.title: Start with macOS Push-to-Talk
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87140 as the narrow first milestone while keeping this broader issue open for custom HTTP, wake/talk, and cross-platform scope.

options.title: Approve broad custom ASR settings
options.body: Sponsor a larger design covering settings UI, endpoint/auth storage, private-network rules, model/language hints, fallback behavior, and mobile/native parity before implementation.

options.title: Keep native voice on platform speech
options.body: Route custom transcription to media-audio/plugin workflows for now and defer native ASR provider work until maintainers want a new core/app seam.

recommendation.title: Start with macOS Push-to-Talk
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87140 as the narrow first milestone while keeping this broader issue open for custom HTTP, wake/talk, and cross-platform scope.

likelyOwner.reason: This issue centers on native macOS voice behavior, and git history points to steipete/Peter Steinberger as the strongest routing candidate for that surface.
